what_this_slice_group_does: Two ruled acts and no retirement. Amendment O, Ruling 1 reclassifies a no-row family off the receipt walk -- a family whose mechanics author no pair-engine row and fold only into the holder's OWN champion rows is PAIR_ONLY under the umbrella's own semantic-authority rule, so its (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferral row was a schedule category error and closes as not_a_gap rather than by a retirement; crit_profile closes that way here, with a machine check that reopens it if a future mechanic of the family ever authors a row. Amendment O, Ruling 2 measures EVERY remaining open deferral row for the same property, once, before any further retirement round, and commits the classification to the schedule receipt where it is diff-gated.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97. Both semantic commits of this group land against the committed baselines with an empty claim set, and the receipt names the baselines anyway: a reader checking that the zero reported below is a zero on the surfaces the campaign gates could not otherwise tell which surfaces those were.

qualifying_population.rule: R-20's second half. The population is enumerated from committed artifacts -- the committed docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json at 6b8011b and scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json's scenario subtrees -- before this group's first src/ edit, and this receipt is the commit that files it. The count cannot be read off the pre-change tree by inspection because a reclassification changes which (family, lane) pairs counter 4 declares, and counter 4's own receipt is a committed artifact whose derived rows a reader would otherwise have to take on trust.
qualifying_population.predicate: Every committed coupled scenario that puts a declaring owner of ANY still-deferred receipt-walk family on a participant. The ten families and their owners are read live from the behaviour catalog over rule_owners(), joined to the frontier's own (family, receipt_walk) deferral rows -- the same join golden_snapshot.receipt_walk_families() makes for the coverage guard -- and the covering predicate is golden_snapshot.covering_scenarios, which is the one home of what covering means.
qualifying_population.why_the_population_is_every_family_and_n: The triage measurement runs the pair engine over every covering scenario of every remaining row, and the reclassification edits the lane table counter 4 derives its declared pairs from. Narrowing the population to crit_profile's two covering rosters would be a guess that the other eight families' scenarios cannot move, which is exactly the guess R-20's second half replaces with an enumeration.
qualifying_population.method: scripts.receipt_walk_schedule.population_size over each selected scenario subtree of the committed coupled baseline.

why_zero_is_predicted_rather_than_hoped: The reclassification's whole src/ reach is the declaration table interpreters._FAMILY_LANES and the unserved-lane row beside it. Neither is on a pricing path: EngineLane.RECEIPT_WALK is absent from item_coverage.ATTACKER_LANES, SCORING_LANES and TARGET_LANES, so no coverage rung, no optimizer eligibility answer and no payload reads it; lanes_for's other two readers are counter 4's own declared-pair set and DEFENSE_FAMILIES, which crit_profile is not in. No interpreter is registered, no mechanic is declared, no row is stamped and no packet is priced. A leaf that moved here would therefore be an occurrence outside the predicted zero and would stop the slice, which is what makes stating the zero a gate rather than a hope.
